intro: You searched for bookkeeping, which usually means you want help keeping your financial records in order, whether you are self-employed, running a small business or simply behind on the paperwork. You want to know who can do this for you, what to expect and how to choose someone suitable. We introduce you to UK bookkeepers who can quote you directly for the work you need.
need_heading: What people searching for bookkeeping usually need
need_lead: Most people looking for bookkeeping want a reliable way to keep their records up to date without doing it all themselves.
needs: You are self-employed and need help with bank reconciliations, invoices and expenses so your records are ready for your tax return.
You run a small business and want someone to take care of VAT returns and management reports on a regular basis.
You have fallen behind with your bookkeeping and need a bookkeeper who can catch up on months of paperwork.
You are starting a new business and need to set up a bookkeeping system, possibly using cloud software, from the beginning.
You want to hand over the day-to-day bookkeeping so you can focus on running your business, while keeping an accountant for year-end accounts and tax advice.
context_heading: What to understand about bookkeeping in the UK
context: Bookkeeping is not a regulated title in the UK, but anyone providing bookkeeping services for a fee must be supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes, either by HMRC or by a professional body. Membership of the Institute of Certified Bookkeepers (ICB) or the Association of Accounting Technicians (AAT) shows a bookkeeper has trained to a recognised standard and agreed to a code of conduct.

Ask whether a bookkeeper holds professional indemnity insurance and which body supervises them. Good bookkeepers are also clear about where their work stops and an accountant's starts, for example on year-end accounts and tax advice.
tell_heading: What to tell us when you enquire
tell: Whether you are self-employed, a partnership or a limited company, as this affects the records you need to keep.
What kind of bookkeeping you need help with, such as bank reconciliations, invoices, VAT returns or management reports.
How often you would like the work done, for example weekly, monthly or quarterly.
Whether you are already using cloud accounting software or paper records, and whether you want to move to cloud software.
If you are behind with your bookkeeping, say how far back the catch-up work needs to go.
Whether you already have an accountant for year-end accounts and tax, so the bookkeeper knows where their work stops.
questions: Which body supervises you for anti-money-laundering purposes?
Do you hold professional indemnity insurance?
Are you a member of the Institute of Certified Bookkeepers (ICB) or the Association of Accounting Technicians (AAT)?
How often would you do the bookkeeping, and does that suit my volume of transactions?
Can you help me catch up if I am behind, and how would you approach that?
Where does your work stop and an accountant's begin, for example on year-end accounts and tax advice?

faqs.q: Do I need a qualified bookkeeper?
faqs.a: Bookkeeping is not a regulated title, but anyone providing bookkeeping services for a fee must be supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes. Membership of the Institute of Certified Bookkeepers (ICB) or the Association of Accounting Technicians (AAT) shows a bookkeeper has trained to a recognised standard and agreed to a code of conduct.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a bookkeeper and an accountant?
faqs.a: A bookkeeper keeps your financial records up to date, from bank reconciliations and invoices to VAT returns and management reports. An accountant typically handles year-end accounts and tax advice. Good bookkeepers are clear about where their work stops and an accountant's starts.

faqs.q: Can a bookkeeper help if I am behind with my records?
faqs.a: Yes, many bookkeepers offer catch-up work to bring your records up to date. Ask about this when you enquire, and explain how far back the work needs to go.

faqs.q: Should I use cloud software for my bookkeeping?
faqs.a: Cloud software lets you see the same numbers as your bookkeeper, which can make communication easier. Ask the bookkeeper whether they work with cloud software and whether they can help you set it up.
